title: Stars, Ravens and Broken Hearts
overview: A song of praise that holds together the God who runs the stars and the weather and the God who rebuilds a ruined city and cares for hurting people.

parts.label: Rebuilding and healing (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: The rebuilt Jerusalem and gathered exiles most likely point to the Jewish people returning home after exile in Babylon. The same God who restores a city is said to tend broken hearts, like someone bandaging a wound.

parts.label: The God who names stars (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: Counting and naming every star was something no human could do, so it shows limitless power and understanding. The psalm's point is that this power is used to lift up the humble and bring down the wicked.

parts.label: Care for creatures, not force (vv. 7-11)
parts.note: God sends the clouds and rain that grow grass on wild hills and feed animals no one looks after, even young ravens when they call. He is not impressed by war horses or a soldier's strong legs, which stood for military might, but by people who respect him and rely on his steady love.

parts.label: A safe and well fed city (vv. 12-14)
parts.note: Zion is another name for Jerusalem, and strong bars on its gates meant protection from attackers. Peace at the borders and the best wheat meant safety and plenty, very concrete gifts, especially if the psalm comes from the time after the return from exile.

parts.label: Snow, ice and thaw (vv. 15-18)
parts.note: God's word is pictured as a fast messenger that brings winter: snow like wool, frost like scattered ash, hail like crumbs. Then the same word sends a warm wind, and the ice melts into flowing water.

parts.label: A word given to Israel (vv. 19-20)
parts.note: The psalm moves from the weather to the laws given to Israel, using the same idea of God's "word" for both. It says no other nation received these laws, and it closes with a final "Praise the LORD."

think: When you think about how vast the universe is, does it make your own struggles feel smaller and less noticed, or does it change how you see them in some other way?
